Apple has waited a very long time to launch its first foldable iPhone, while Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series is already in its eighth generation.

Apple originally had good reason to hold off a little longer, but Samsung's latest user experience suggests the iPhone maker's timing is spot on...

Apple's long wait

Samsung was one of the earliest companies to heavily push foldable smartphones, but it soon found it had moved too fast. The first-generation Samsung Galaxy Fold had an extremely fragile screen prone to damage, and Samsung ultimately had to pull it from the market.

Meanwhile, Apple has been patiently waiting for display technology to mature to the point where it is significantly more durable and shows no obvious crease when unfolded. Reports indicate Apple even sent its own design engineers to help Samsung achieve this goal.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 — the timing is right

We mentioned last month that the display used in the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is very likely to be extremely close to the one that will be used in the iPhone Ultra. Our sister site 9to5Google discovered that it has truly delivered on its promise — the crease in the middle of the screen is almost invisible when unfolded.

However, it's not just that Samsung has finally got the display technology right; consumer demand also seems to have finally caught up. According to 9to5Google, initial demand for the Fold 8 is three times that of its predecessor.

This figure follows on from last year's 50% growth in demand.

Of course, these two things are likely related — a crease-free screen greatly boosts appeal — but factoring in last year's growth, foldable phones have been around for quite some time now, and more people are beginning to see the benefits of this form factor.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to debut next month alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. Expectations are that this new device will quickly capture roughly 25% of the entire foldable smartphone market.
